item.title: [Representative figure added] Ghd7‑triggered transcriptional regulation for synergistically improving rice eating quality and yield
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Topologically robust programmable processing arrays using light and matter skyrmions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78249-7

Optical skyrmions offer a route to scalable photonic computing via perturbation-resilient topological invariants of the optical field. Here, authors introduce a platform-independent architecture for skyrmion-based processing arrays, built around a library of topologically robust optical primitives.

item.title: Reward function compression facilitates goal-dependent reinforcement learning
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78295-1

People can learn to achieve arbitrary goals, but this flexibility requires cognitive effort. Here, the authors show that the brain resolves this by progressively compressing complex reward information into simplified rules, freeing up working memory to facilitate reinforcement learning.

item.title: Earlier green-up exacerbates northern vegetation sensitivity to flash drought
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78296-0

Flash droughts can rapidly reduce vegetation growth, but the role of spring phenology is unclear. The authors show that earlier green-up increases vegetation sensitivity to flash drought across much of the Northern Hemisphere ecosystems.

item.title: Error semitransparent universal control of a bosonic logical qubit
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78317-y

Error transparency is an alternative approach to quantum fault-tolerance relying on multi-body Hamiltonians whose evolution is unaffected - to first order - by noise. Here, the authors show a dynamic encoding subspace framework achieving universal control of Bosonic logical qubits with error semitransparent gates, correcting most single-photon loss errors in the Bosonic mode during logical gate operations.

item.title: Cooperative outer-surface recognition extends host–guest chemistry for high-capacity molecular separation beyond cavity inclusion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78531-8

The separation of azeotropic and structurally similar mixtures remains challenging for conventional porous materials. Here the authors introduce a conceptual extension of classical host–guest chemistry that moves beyond exclusive cavity-based recognition to exploit cooperative interactions at the outer surface of macrocyclic hosts.

item.title: Olaparib plus tremelimumab in women with recurrent ovarian cancer and a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation: a phase I/II study
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78395-y

Response rate to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in ovarian cancer remains low and combinatorial strategies are needed. Here the authors report the results of a phase I/II study of the PARP inhibitor olaparib and the anti-CTLA4 antibody tremelimumab in women with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer and a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.

item.title: Bacterial toxin sensing induces transient inflammasome-dependent innate immune memory that improves survival during sepsis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78499-5

This study shows that the bacterial toxin CNF1 can train innate immune cells to respond more effectively to subsequent infections, revealing a form of immune memory that improves survival during sepsis in mice.

item.title: APOE2 attenuates APOE4-associated amyloid pathology and related toxicity in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78407-x

Chen and colleagues use a heterozygous mouse model carrying human APOE2 and APOE4 alleles to show that APOE2 attenuates APOE4- associated effects on brain amyloid pathology and related cellular and molecular changes.

item.title: [Representative figure added] A spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic atlas reveals fertilization-induced auxin signaling driving strawberry fruit set and development
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: High-resolution binding data of TFIID and cofactors show promoter-specific differences
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77758-9

Here, the authors use ChIP-nexus to map all TFIID subunits and cofactors across the Drosophila genome at base pair resolution, revealing a general TFIID organization across promoter types with promoter-specific TBP and NC2 binding.

item.title: Author Correction: Ferroelectric ultraviolet photodetector material with ultrafast response speed
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78436-6

Author Correction: Ferroelectric ultraviolet photodetector material with ultrafast response speed

item.title: A cytidine deaminase biodegrader sensitises multiple cancer types to deoxycytidine analogue-based chemotherapies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78315-0

Deoxycytidine (dC) analogues form the basis of many chemotherapeutic agents but their efficacy is limited by cytidine deaminase-mediated inactivation. Here, the authors develop an intracellular biodegrader targeting cytidine deaminase, capable of sensitising multiple cancer types to dC analogues.

item.title: Neonatal overfeeding accelerates age-related sarcopenia and metabolic disorders through lifelong gut mucosa and microbiota programming in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78216-2

Here, the authors demonstrate that neonatal overfeeding in mice shortens lifespan and accelerates late-life muscle loss. This originates from persistent gut mucus defects and depleted Akkermansia muciniphila, revealing a targetable developmental origin for sarcopenia.

item.title: Trillion-scale integrated framework for high-throughput materials databases and seamless sharing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78223-3

A new computing framework builds large-scale materials databases under resource constraints, with major gains in efficiency, storage, and query speed plus edge-device deployment. A ten-trillion-scale HEA database was built in one week.

item.title: Meta-analysis of empirical evidence on biodiversity and the risk of asthma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77643-5

Biodiversity loss is associated with several adverse health effects. Here, the authors report the results of a meta-analysis investigating the effect of exposure to high environmental and human biodiversity on the risk of asthma.

item.title: The chromatin-organizer Satb1 modulates regulatory T cell activity within the tumor microenvironment
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78360-9

Identifying differences in Treg subtypes to disrupt the activities of tumor-promoting Tregs remains a challenge. Here, the authors report that Treg expression of SATB1 distinguishes pro-tumorigenic Tregs from Tregs that maintain immune homeostasis.

item.title: A selectivity filter in Tim17 mediates intramitochondrial protein sorting
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77990-3

Tim17 forms the protein-conducting channel of the mitochondrial inner membrane translocase. Here, authors show that the N-terminus of Tim17 constitutes a negatively charged selectivity filter to facilitate the intramitochondrial protein sorting.

item.title: The WorkReach model for urban work location choices through economic complexity and informality
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78293-3

The WorkReach model captures how economic opportunity and informality shape commuting. Analyzing four major cities, this study shows that measuring job access by perceived benefits, not just proximity, exposes hidden socioeconomic disparities.

item.title: Sub-stoichiometric degradation is dispensable for potent PROTACs as demonstrated by irreversible covalent BTK degraders
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78239-9

Protein degraders are thought to require repeated rounds of action, so molecules binding their target irreversibly were considered unsuitable. Here, the authors describe a covalent BTK degrader active at sub-nanomolar doses in cells and show what governs its potency.

item.title: The Wnt co-receptor Arrow-LRP5/6 is required for planar cell polarity establishment in Drosophila
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78357-4

The LRP5/6 Wnt co-receptor was thought to be specific to Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Our work in Drosophila shows that it is equally critical in Wnt/planar cell polarity signaling, also promoting activity of the common downstream effector Dishevelled.

item.title: Game theory driven multi-agent framework mitigates language model hallucination
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78213-5

Lightweight AI models can be unreliable in specialized scientific tasks. Here, the authors introduce G-Frame, which uses game theory to coordinate multiple AI agents, automate data generation and training, and reduce hallucinations.

item.title: Divergent interfaces and convergent outcome in the structural basis of HIV-2 Vif antagonism of APOBEC3H
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78197-2

HIV-2 Vif antagonizes host APOBEC3 restriction factors, but its mechanism remains poorly defined. Here, authors report the cryoEM structure of HIV-2 Vif bound to APOBEC3H, revealing a CBFβ-mediated interface distinct from HIV-1 Vif.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Near-atomistic simulations reveal the molecular principles that control chromatin structure and phase separation
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Real-time visualization of G2L4 reverse transcriptase in DNA repair via microhomology-mediated end joining
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78460-6

The error-prone microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) pathway is important for double strand break repair. Here, the authors use high-speed atomic force microscopy to visualize how the Pseudomonas aeruginosa chromosomally encoded group II intron-like reverse transcriptase (G2L4 RT) act on MMEJ substrates.

item.title: Ultrathin high-performance circular polarizers based on MoOCl<sub>2</sub>/NbOCl<sub>2</sub> van der Waals heterostructures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78564-z

Circularly polarized light can be used in several applications, but normally requires bulky optical components. Here, the authors report the realization of sub-micron-thick circular polarizers based on the natural phase modulation capability of NbOCl2 and polarization selectivity of MoOCl2 crystals, showing their integration into a LED chip.

item.title: Embryonic origin of cancer in newborn twins
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78178-5

Identical twins with the same cancer can reveal how childhood tumours arise and spread before birth. Here, the authors use whole-genome sequencing of tumour, normal and placental tissues to show that a sarcoma that originated in one twin spread to the other in utero, and trace early embryonic lineages that contributed differently to the twins and placenta.

item.title: Distinct T cell correlates of COVID-19 risk before and after a second booster in previously SARS-CoV-2 infected versus naïve COVAIL trial participants
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78444-6

Vaccines to SARS-CoV-2 clearly stimulate virus specific T cell and antibody responses but T cell-mediated protection is challenging to show. Here the authors use PBMC samples from an open-label clinical trial of different prototype and variant-specific COVID-19 vaccine boosters to examine the function and phenotype of T cell populations and how T cell response levels associate with risk of, and with protection against, symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.

item.title: MOF-mediated cascade photoreactions under nanoconfinement for defluorination of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78192-7

Here, authors report a nanoconfinement strategy to encapsulate a MOF photocatalyst within a graphene aerogel matrix. This not only allows cascade reduction-oxidation reactions but also provides kinetic and thermodynamic advantages for efficient defluorination of various PFASs.

item.title: Symmetry-engineered and electrically tunable in-plane anomalous Hall effect in oxide heterostructures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78350-x

The authors demonstrate that engineering crystal symmetry in oxide heterostructures creates a robust in-plane anomalous Hall effect, enabling direct readout of in-plane magnetization and a wide range of fully reversible electrical ON/OFF switching.

item.title: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of (hetero)aromatic frameworks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78282-6

Catalytic asymmetric dearomative cycloaddition offers an attractive route to chiral polycycles, but achieving divergent and site-selective transformations across diverse polycyclic aromatics remains challenging. Here, the authors report a vinylidene ortho-quinone methide platform that enables predictable, highly selective dearomative cycloadditions of diverse (hetero)polycyclic aromatics.

item.title: Water-oil interfacial kinetics control enables water-based organic solar cells with 12.59% certified efficiency
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78233-1

The practical applications of environmentally friendly water-based organic solar cells are hindered by low device performance. Bi et al. develop an interfacial-tension-mediated regulation strategy to improve nanoparticle-derived film formation, achieving a power conversion efficiency of 12.64%.

item.title: High potential contribution of intercropping to soybean and maize self-sufficiency in Europe
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78206-4

Domestic production of maize and soybeans in the EU currently falls short of demand. This study finds that adoption of maize-soybean intercropping could improve soybean self-sufficiency by 25−91% but also contribute to EU maize demand by 50−145%.

item.title: A generative diffusion framework for physically consistent 3D turbulence
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78265-7

Three-dimensional turbulence contains complex multiscale fluctuations that challenge even state-of-the-art generative models. Here, the authors develop a generative diffusion framework that produces physically consistent 3D turbulence with accurate multiscale statistics.

item.title: Coherent terahertz control of metastable magnetization in FePS<sub>3</sub>
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78164-x

Light-driven phonons offer a route to nonequilibrium phases, yet coherent, on demand control of such phases has been hard to achieve. Here, Ilyas, Luo, Ning and co-authors show that the timing of two terahertz pulses sets the amplitude of a metastable magnetization in FePS3, through anharmonic coupling of infrared active phonons to a magnetization inducing Raman mode.

item.title: Large-scale proteomics identifies circulating markers of pulmonary pressure and pulmonary hypertension risk
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78432-w

By integrating proteomics, genetics and imaging, this study identifies candidate blood biomarkers of pulmonary hypertension, implicates NOTCH3 in disease development, and defines distinct biological subtypes of individuals at risk for this condition.

item.title: Ghd7‑triggered transcriptional regulation for synergistically improving rice eating quality and yield
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78253-x

Rice breeders struggle to boost yield and eating quality simultaneously as the two traits often work against each other. Here, the authors identify a CCT domain transcription regulator encoding gene Ghd7 in determining rice grain amylose content and functioning in balancing starch and protein to coordinate yield and quality.

item.title: PSHIC reveals allele-specific chromatin organization by phasing-free structural modeling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78098-4

PSHIC reconstructs parent-specific 3D genome organization from standard Hi-C data without phased genetic variants. It outperforms existing methods and recovers validated features of X inactivation, imprinting and gene regulation.

item.title: Coordination ring-opening transamidation copolymerization of cyclic lactones and lactams towards circular and biodegradable poly(ester amide) adhesives
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78220-6

The direct copolymerization of lactones and lactams to produce poly(ester amide)s is a challenge. Here, the authors report the titanium catalyzed ring-opening transamidation polymerization of ε-caprolactone and ε-caprolactam to produce biodegradable poly(ester amide)s with good adhesive properties.

item.title: Narrowing urban heat disparities alongside faster greening in low-income neighborhoods across cities in the United States
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78468-y

This study finds that heat disparities between high- and low-income neighborhoods narrowed across 55 U.S. cities from 1986 to 2020, alongside faster greening in disadvantaged neighborhoods, although substantial inequalities persisted.

item.title: Reframing decentralized diagnostics with a programmable multi-dimensional microfluidic system
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77744-1

Decentralized diagnostics has the potential to improve health equity as well as support a more rapid response to disease outbreaks. Here authors present SID-WAVES, a multimodal microfluidic platform which allows ‘sample-in, results-out’ detection of both nucleic acid and protein biomarkers.

item.title: A multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of dasatinib in T follicular helper cell lymphomas
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78100-z

T follicular helper cell lymphomas (TFHL) depend on T cell receptor (TCR) signaling propagated by tyrosine kinases. Here, the authors conduct a phase 2 clinical trial of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib in TFHL, not meeting the prespecified primary endpoint (ORR = 23.5%), but correlating response with TCR signaling mutations.

item.title: Global scale river discharge and mean depth from radar altimetry and model
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78275-5

This study combines multi-mission satellite altimetry with global discharge reanalysis to derive near-global river rating curves and effective channel depths at more than 26,000 locations worldwide, enabling discharge estimation and hydraulic characterization across gauged and ungauged rivers.

item.title: Fear learning–induced brain dynamics predict individual extinction memory expression following transcranial magnetic stimulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78345-8

Zhang et al. show that fear learning reshapes spontaneous brain activity and that these changes can predict individual differences in how extinction memories are later expressed following TMS-modulated extinction.

item.title: TransGram for heterogeneity-aware transcriptome reconstruction from long read RNA-Seq data
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78013-x

Long-read RNA sequencing datasets exhibit heterogeneity that affects transcript reconstruction. Here, the authors characterize this heterogeneity and develop TransGram, which adapts reconstruction to different data types to improve accuracy.

item.title: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78126-3

A multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform was established by conjugating NA inhibitors and Fc domain. AVCs cross-link flu viruses, blocking entry and release. Trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate outperformed clinical drugs in mice.

item.title: A family of small proteins links c-di-GMP riboswitch signaling with sporulation in Clostridioides difficile
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78452-6

The second messenger c-di-GMP inhibits sporulation in the pathogenic bacterium Clostridioides difficile through unclear mechanisms. Here, Badilla Lobo et al. show that the expression of sporulation genes is modulated by a family of small membrane-associated proteins encoded by genes that are controlled by c-diGMP-regulated riboswitches.

item.title: A CCL21 gene-modified dendritic cell vaccine combined with pembrolizumab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a phase I trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78130-7

Feasibility and safety profile of intratumoral administration of a DC vaccine overexpressing CCL21 (CCL21-DC) have been previously reported in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here the authors report safety, clinical outcomes and immunological correlates of a phase I trial of CCL21-DC in combination with anti-PD1 pembrolizumab in patients with advanced NSCLC.

item.title: Volitional control of wearable robots
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78416-w

This Comment motivates the development of human–machine interfaces that decode spinal motor neuron activity and resulting muscle force information in moving humans. Such interfaces could enable users across the neuromuscular functional spectrum to volitionally control wearable robots with muscle-like behaviour.

item.title: Thermally programmed disassembly and reconstruction of 2D polymer platelets via melting-governed crystallization-driven self-assembly
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77973-4

‘Crystallization-driven self-assembly is a useful tool for the synthesis of polymer nanostructures with precise dimensions, but the melting behavior of polymer crystals grown in solution has remained largely unexplored. Here, the authors show that melting temperature is a structurally sensitive descriptor and an active design parameter for 2D platelets.’

item.title: Monolithic three-dimensionally integrated memristor-thin-film transistor for electrically programmable multimode reservoir computing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78364-5

Current reservoir computing hardware is efficient but limited by fixed dynamics. Shim et al. report a monolithically integrated memristor-transistor reservoir with electrically programmable temporal dynamics, supporting multiple temporal processing modes for motion recognition and biomedical signal classification.

item.title: Top-down semantic predictions align phonetic neuronal dynamics in human superior temporal gyrus
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77942-x

How semantic information influences phonetic processing during speech perception remains unclear. Here, the authors show that semantic predictions reshape phonetic representations in human temporal cortex at the level of neuronal population activity.

item.title: DCAF7 regulates hematopoietic stem cell function and differentiation through polycomb repressive complex 1 modulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78299-x

This study identifies DCAF7 as a new regulator of blood stem cells showing how it controls chromatin to preserve stem cell function with implications for understanding normal and malignant blood formation.

item.title: The structural dynamics and molecular coupling in the slow inactivation of a prokaryotic voltage-gated sodium channel
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78235-z

Slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels is important for regulating cellular excitability. Here the authors probe the conformational dynamics in the selectivity filter using smFRET and reveal the critical residue pair that mediates conformational communication between the primary and slow inactivation gates

item.title: Enantioselective palladium-catalyzed carbonylation of gem-dibromoalkenes to chiral benzo[7]annulenes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78226-0

The authors report a palladium-catalyzed asymmetric monocarbonylation of conformationally rigid, prochiral benzo[7]annulenebased gemdibromoalkenes, furnishing inherently chiral tetrasubstituted benzo[7]annulene derivatives with excellent yields and high enantioselectivities.

item.title: Design principle for mitigating moisture-induced degradation in 2D halide perovskites
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78054-2

In humid air, 2D perovskites degrade into various lead-rich nonperovskite phases. The easier it is for such phases to form, the faster degradation proceeds. By tuning a 2D perovskite’s molecular cations to not accommodate any lead-rich phases, stability can be markedly improved.

item.title: Sustainability cost of defect engineering in color centers for quantum communications
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78261-x

Sustainable manufacturing is becoming an increasingly important consideration for emerging quantum technologies. Here, the authors assess the environmental, chemical, human-health, and economic impacts of defect engineering strategies for color-center platforms used in quantum communications, highlighting trade-offs between quantum functionality and resource demands while identifying lower-impact solutions.

item.title: Bulk mesophases modeling of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78039-1

Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals are an emerging class of materials in which nematic orientational order coexists with spontaneous macroscopic polarization. Vats et al. develop a free-energy framework to rationalize their bulk structures and predict potential bend-instability-driven mesophases.

item.title: Near-atomistic simulations reveal the molecular principles that control chromatin structure and phase separation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78050-6

Russell et al. introduce a 10 × faster, chemically detailed chromatin model bridging molecular and genomic scales, revealing how DNA sequence, spacing and histone acetylation govern chromatin folding and phase separation.

item.title: Anti-Kasha fluorescence and persistent room-temperature phosphorescence from a nearly flat non-symmetric polycyclic hydrocarbon
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78107-6

Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are efficient emitters, but achieving desirable properties can be challenging. Here, the authors report the development of monohomotruxene, a nonsymmetric compound with anti-kasha and ultra-long blue phosphorescence.

item.title: Different concentrations of atropine in children with high myopia: a 2-year multicenter double-blind, randomized controlled trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77797-2

Here the authors report the results of a multicenter, double-blind, randomized-controlled trial that evaluates the effect and safety of different concentration atropine eyedrops (0.01%, 0.04%, 0.10%) for myopia control in children with high myopia. The findings show that nightly use of 0.10% atropine eye drops for 24 months mitigated myopia progression with an acceptable safety profile.

item.title: Immune correlates of protection are exposure-dependent: evidence from the Dominican Republic
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78427-7

This study shows that antibody levels linked to protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection vary with transmission intensity, suggesting immune correlates of protection depend on exposure context.

item.title: Author Correction: DNA methylation-free Arabidopsis reveals crucial roles of DNA methylation in regulating gene expression and development
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78327-w

Author Correction: DNA methylation-free Arabidopsis reveals crucial roles of DNA methylation in regulating gene expression and development

item.title: Author Correction: A mutually antagonistic mechanism mediated by RNA m<sup>6</sup>A modification in plant-virus interactions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78523-8

Author Correction: A mutually antagonistic mechanism mediated by RNA m6A modification in plant-virus interactions

item.title: A model of brain function to predict tau across Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78300-7

Researchers developed a machine learning model using FDG-PET imaging to accurately predict Alzheimer’s-type tau pathology across spectrums of aging and dementia, providing a novel framework to estimate tau burden non-invasively.

item.title: AI-accelerated scalable synthesis of nanocrystals for cost-effective photovoltaics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78268-4

The commercialization of perovskite nanocrystals requires low-cost synthesis and processing. Zhao et al. developed an AI-accelerated framework to optimize the FAPbI3 nanocrystal synthesis under room-temperature, achieving a production cost of US$ 2.16 g−1 with a power conversion efficiency of 19.37%.

item.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals microenvironmental heterogeneity in osteoarthritic subchondral bone
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77518-9

Subchondral bone remodeling is increasingly implicated in osteoarthritis, but its spatial organization remain incompletely understood. This study provides a high-resolution spatial map of subchondral bone and identifies conserved spatial architectures, revealing distinct microenvironmental states and candidate signaling pathways associated with subchondral bone sclerosis.

item.title: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ-driven uveal melanomas
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77999-8

Uveal melanoma (UM) is often driven by mutations in GNAQ. Here, authors identify p300 as a synthetic lethal target in GNAQ-mutant UM and show that p300 inhibition impairs tumour growth and metastasis.

item.title: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78190-9

In this study, Jose Molto and colleagues report data from a randomised open-label clinical trial showing of first-line dolutegravir/lamivudine treatment for HIV-1. They report that the treatment reaches lymph nodes and regions containing HIV-positive cells, which strengthens evidence for antiviral exposure within a key anatomical HIV reservoir.

item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Author Correction: Whole-brain, all-optical interrogation of neuronal dynamics underlying gut and vascular interoception in zebrafish
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78324-z

Author Correction: Whole-brain, all-optical interrogation of neuronal dynamics underlying gut and vascular interoception in zebrafish

item.title: Author Correction: Hyperbranched dielectric polymer networks exhibiting giant energy storage density at 250 °C.
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78332-z

Author Correction: Hyperbranched dielectric polymer networks exhibiting giant energy storage density at 250 °C.

item.title: Author Correction: Clinical translation and engineering challenges of soft robotic cardiac sleeves for heart failure
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78328-9

Author Correction: Clinical translation and engineering challenges of soft robotic cardiac sleeves for heart failure

item.title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77562-5

Aqueous zinc-ion batteries promise safe energy storage but suffer from dendrites and side reactions. Here, authors engineer a zwitterionic fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte to suppress these issues, enabling durable, dendrite free, Ah-level pouch cells.

item.title: Genome mining of the tumor microbiome reveals biosynthetic diversity and potential pathology-modulating metabolites
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78166-9

Here, Pulliam and colleagues characterize the metabolites encoded by tumor-inhabiting microbes and their potential role in cancer pathology.

item.title: Repurposing the evolutionary fitness of marine bacteria for water-conserving conversion of lignin-derived carbon
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78209-1

Reverting waste carbon into chemicals with minimal freshwater use is essential for a sustainable future. Here, the authors engineer the marine bacterium R. nubinhibens, by decoupling bioproduction from central metabolism to convert lignin into chemicals with seawater as a water source.

item.title: Author Correction: Surveillance of avian influenza through bird guano in remote regions of the global south to uncover transmission dynamics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78237-x

Author Correction: Surveillance of avian influenza through bird guano in remote regions of the global south to uncover transmission dynamics

item.title: Low contact resistance and high current density in ballistic p-type transistors based on oxygen-doped WSe<sub>2</sub> monolayers
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78157-w

The realization of high-performance p-type transistors is essential for the realization of next-generation 2D electronics. Here, the authors report the realization of oxygen-doped p-type monolayer WSe2 transistors with hole mobility over 200 cm2 V−1 s−1, contact resistance down to 104 Ω·μm and saturation current densities up to 1635 μA/μm at a drain voltage of -1.2 V.

item.title: Cell-autonomous restoration of splicing homeostasis and RP11 phenotype in patient-derived RPE and retinal organoids by PRPF31.AAV gene therapy
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78065-z

PRPF31 gene therapy restores RNA splicing and reverses cellular dysfunction in patient-derived retinal models of retinitis pigmentosa. The treatment cures advanced cellular defects, highlighting a wide window for clinical intervention.

item.title: Generative design of high-fidelity microstructures using physics-aware machine learning
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78118-3

This study uses physics-aware AI to generate high-fidelity microstructures beyond existing data distributions, resulting in a bimodal grain structure that enables improved strength and ductility.

item.title: Programmable DNA protonuclei reveal environmental context on protein phase separation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78144-1

Protein phase separation is often investigated in dilute solution, meaning that the influence of the crowded environmental context of cells is often overlooked. Here, the authors introduce a programmable DNA-based platform to probe the phase behavior of proteins within a more biomimetic environment.

item.title: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77925-y

In this exploratory randomized trial, the monoclonal antibody AER002 was safe but did not improve clinical or biomarker outcomes in Long COVID. Post-hoc findings suggest baseline antibody levels and drug exposure may inform future studies.

item.title: Magnetic Electroluminescent response as a predictive indicator of operational lifetime in phosphorescent blue OLEDs
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78180-x

Predicting the operational lifetime of blue organic light-emitting diodes without destructive and lengthy aging tests remains challenging. Ji et al. identify a magnetic-field electroluminescence response that quantitatively predicts operational lifetime.

item.title: Stress homogenization enabled by a layered composite electrolyte for high-performance all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78129-0

Mechanical stress limits the lifetime of solid-state lithium metal batteries. Here, authors reveal that the mechanical electrochemical coupling governs battery cycling and develop a layered solid electrolyte that enables uniform lithium deposition and durable solid-state batteries.

item.title: WeedNet: a foundation model-based global-to-local AI approach for weed species identification and classification
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78044-4

Weeds consistently threaten crop yields worldwide, making early and accurate identification essential for effective management. Trained on 14 million images representing 1,593 weed species, WeedNet achieved 91% global accuracy and, through global-to-local fine-tuning, reached 97% accuracy for Iowa weeds.

item.title: Metabolization of human milk oligosaccharides by Streptococcus pneumoniae
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77970-7

It is unclear whether human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) can be used as a nutrient source by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Here, Bacher et al. report that these bacteria can metabolize several HMOs, identify genes and pathways involved in the process, and show that a non-metabolizable HMO inhibits pneumococcal adherence to host cells.

item.title: Powder-to-membrane transformation affording 2D/3D COF membranes for molecular separations
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78068-w

Processing covalent organic framework (COF) powders into application-ready membranes with precise separation capacity remains challenging. Here, the authors demonstrate a dual-drive strategy that drives macroscopic structural variation and transforms COF powders into defect-free membranes.

item.title: RuPHOTACs provide photocontrol over protein degradation with optimized properties for biological applications
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78110-x

PROTACs offer a powerful strategy to eliminate disease-relevant proteins, but off-target activity in healthy tissues remains a major challenge. Here, the authors introduce Ruthenium-based PHOToActivated Chimeras (RuPHOTACs), a new class of light-responsive PROTACs that remain inactive until triggered by low-energy light.

item.title: Ligand engineering enables an alkaline iron-chromium redox flow battery
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77810-8

Iron-chromium redox flow batteries are promising for long-duration energy storage but suffer from sluggish chromium(II/III) chemistry. Here, authors use a strong-field ligand to unlock a chromium(III/IV) posolyte and establish a 1.15 V alkaline iron chromium redox flow battery.

item.title: Chlorophyll as a sustainable crosslinking strategy for engineering highly compressible hydrogels
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77673-z

Hydrogels with high deformation and resilience are desirable for applications such as injectable cardiac patches. Here, authors provide a strategy using chlorophyll as a physical crosslinker to engineer highly compressible hydrogels.

item.title: Domino effect enables dynamic electronic structure evolution for stable and efficient water purification
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78263-9

The authors develop a domino catalytic system that dynamically reconstructs active sites’ electronic structure, lowering reaction barriers and inhibiting metal leaching for efficient and durable water purification.

item.title: Quantitative changes in 3D contact predict changes in enhancer-promoter regulation upon cohesin depletion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77582-1

By depleting cohesin, the authors show that changes in 3D enhancer-promoter contacts alter enhancer regulatory effects. But only a subset of enhancer-promoter pairs shows weakened 3D contacts, explaining why only some genes change in expression.

item.title: A role for selective ER autophagy in gametogenic rejuvenation revealed by high-throughput lifespan profiling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77993-0

Gametogenesis fully resets lifespan, although how this is achieved is unclear. Here, Spiri et al. developed a high-throughput assay to study this rejuvenation event in yeast, revealing selective autophagy of the ER as a key molecular mechanism.

item.title: An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77968-1

Electronic structure calculations usually need a good starting guess, often unavailable for strongly correlated systems. The authors develop an auto-initializing algorithm that efficiently finds accurate ground states from random Slater determinants.

item.title: Waned mantle upwelling contributes to a heavily deformed northern smooth plains on Mercury
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74974-1

Waned mantle upwelling contributes to a heavily deformed northern smooth plains on Mercury

item.title: Structural mechanisms underlying resistance to Switch-II pocket inhibitors in KRAS
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78133-4

This study explores how clinically observed KRAS resistance mutations alter drug-binding interactions and dynamics of the Switch-II pocket while preserving oncogenic signaling, providing a structural framework for developing more durable KRAS inhibitors.

item.title: Unexpected stabilization of a single-q charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe2
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78072-0

The authors show that the subcomponents of the charge density wave in 1T-TiSe₂ are unequal and set in one by one, beginning with an unexpected unidirectional state.

item.title: A SAGA-like AP2-P-ARP1-GCN5 transcriptional complex targets pathogenesis-associated genes during the blood-stage development of Babesia gibsoni
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78127-2

This study characterizes a novel SAGA-like epigenetic regulatory module in Babesia gibsoni, composed of the ApiAP2 transcription factor AP2-P, ARP1 and histone acetyltransferase GCN5. This complex modulates chromatin accessibility and binds specific genomic motifs to control the expression of genes involved in parasite invasion, antigenic variation, drug resistance and stage conversion, critically supporting parasite blood-stage growth and pathogenicity.

item.title: Religious celibacy is linked to marriage and wealth transmission practices across different world religions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78153-0

Lifelong religious celibacy has been linked to sibling competition over parental wealth. Here, the authors show that celibacy is linked to marriage patterns, and its prevalence among men and women is related to which sex faces higher marriage payments.

item.title: Exploring Li growth modes in Li metal electrodes using X-ray nano-tomography
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78182-9

The growth of porous, weakly connected structures in Li electrodes is directly linked to the poor cycle life of Li-metal batteries. Here, the authors use in situ nano-tomography to track the evolution of these structures and understand their growth mechanism.

item.title: Deep-learning single-cell profiling uncovers interbacterial and drug-driven reshaping of pathogen virulence
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77989-w

This study introduces MALVINA, a deep-learning platform that measures bacterial invasion and DNA damage in individual human cells, revealing how bacterial interactions and commonly used drugs reshape pathogen virulence.

item.title: Building-block synthesis as a determinant of antibiotic persistence
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78277-3

Reduced antibiotic target activity is a major driver of antibiotic treatment failure. While this has mostly been linked to the presence of low-energy bacteria, a recent study by Taher and colleagues suggests that reduced building-block synthesis can also promote antibiotic survival during nitrogen starvation — a route distinct from energy limitation.

item.title: mHolmes improves cross anatomical cadaveric microbiome forecasting for postmortem interval estimation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77510-3

This study presents mHolmes, a transfer-learning framework that forecasts postmortem microbiome changes across body sites, improving postmortem interval estimation and highlighting microbial features with forensic potential.

item.title: Metal cofactor-level chassis engineering enables aerobic expression of tungsten formate dehydrogenases in Escherichia coli
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78159-8

Tungsten-dependent enzyme production is limited by complex metal cofactor requirements and poor compatibility with expression hosts. Here the authors engineer E. coli to support the aerobic production of various tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases.

item.title: Structural basis of stepwise G protein activation by the viral chemokine receptor US28
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78122-7

GPCRs are crucial drug targets, but the structural steps of G protein activation remain elusive. Here, using cryo-EM, the authors capture plausible intermediate states of a viral GPCR-human Gq complex, suggesting a stepwise activation mechanism.

item.title: mRNA-1273 SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in people with HIV: an immune correlates analysis of CD4 + T cell responses in the multicenter CoVPN 3008 observational study
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77995-y

In people with HIV and hybrid immunity (prior SARS-CoV-2 infection + vaccination), CD4 + T cell responses at one month post-vaccination correlate inversely with risk of COVID-19 over 6 months.

item.title: Author Correction: Unified bilayer membranes with mechanically reinforced interface for stage-adaptive bone regeneration
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78171-y

Author Correction: Unified bilayer membranes with mechanically reinforced interface for stage-adaptive bone regeneration

item.title: Environmental stochasticity reduces human planning effort
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78023-9

The real world is stochastic, making it difficult to know when planning is worthwhile. Here the authors show that as stochasticity increases, people spend less effort planning and adopt simpler, less value-sensitive decision policies.

item.title: Author Correction: Nanoscale exchange-bias magnetic tunnel junctions enabled memristive synapse and leaky-integrate-fire neuron for neuromorphic computing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78298-y

Author Correction: Nanoscale exchange-bias magnetic tunnel junctions enabled memristive synapse and leaky-integrate-fire neuron for neuromorphic computing

item.title: Nighttime warming dominates the thermal evolution of lakes across China
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78114-7

A 25-year analysis of 613 Chinese lakes shows that lake warming is largely driven by nighttime temperature increases, with atmospheric longwave radiation and human activities reinforcing this trend.

item.title: “Descending Enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus gate sex-biased control of micturition”
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77949-4

The neural control of LUT (lower urinary tract) function is not fully understood. Here authors demonstrate that transcriptionally distinct enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus are recruited during voiding to selectively control external urethral sphincter relaxation and regulate urinary behaviors in a sex-specific manner.

item.title: The plasma protease inhibitor ITIH4 forms oligomeric complexes and senses broader proteolytic activity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78173-w

Using electron microscopy, the authors describe the conformational changes induced when the plasma protease inhibitor ITIH4 is cleaved and activated. Moreover, oligomerization of cleaved ITIH4 is shown not to impact protease inhibition.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Resonating-valence-bond superconductor from small Fermi surface in twisted bilayer graphene
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Manipulation of ferromagnetism with a light-driven nonlinear Edelstein-Zeeman field
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77965-4

Ultrafast non-thermal control of magnetism is a major goal of spintronics, however, in centrosymmetric materials, symmetry typically forbids direct control via electric fields. Here, Lv, Meese and coauthors use the non-linear Edelstein effect to create a non-equilibrium magnetic density in the van der Waals magnetic semiconductor Cr2Ge2Te6.

item.title: Branched-type nanocluster-junction fluorofluidic-gels for interface-adaptive thermal conduction and mechanical resistance
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78046-2

‘Conventional thermal interface materials often suffer from a certain degree of mismatch between their thermal conductivity and contact thermal resistance. Here the authors develop a thermal interface fluorofluidic-gel with a branched-type nanocluster-junction network exhibiting high thermal conductivity and low contact thermal resistance.

item.title: Emergent charge crystallization and frustration in a particle anti-spin ice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77905-2

Artificial spin ices are a versatile platform for realizing geometrically frustrated states. Here, the authors demonstrate an anti-spin ice made of trapped colloids which experience tunable isotropic attractive interactions and which invert the conventional ice rule paradigm.

item.title: Efficient transport kinetics of indirect excitons in van der Waals heterostructure
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77967-2

Here, the authors investigate the transport kinetics of indirect excitons (IXs) in a MoSe2/WSe2 van der Waals heterostructure, and observe anomalously high IX mobility, consistent with IX superfluidity.

item.title: Global spatiotemporal dynamics of mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections over the past three decades
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77197-6

Long-term mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections is poorly characterised worldwide. Here, authors analyse data from 204 countries and territories, revealing divergent trajectories by region, pathogen, and pandemic period.

item.title: Alteromonas macleodii breaches the diatom frustule triggering protoplast emergence and programmed necrosis-like death in Thalassiosira rotula
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78079-7

In this study, the authors show that the marine bacterium Alteromonas macleodii exploits the diatom Thalassiosira rotula by triggering programmed necrosis-like cell death. By forcing cells out of their silica shells and lysing them, this interaction may affect ocean carbon cycling.

item.title: Microglia regulate nucleus accumbens synaptic development and circuit function underlying threat avoidance behaviors in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77487-z

Microglial synapse removal has been heavily studied. Here, the authors reveal roles for microglia in synapse formation by showing that absence of nucleus accumbens microglia during development reduces synapse number and alters avoidance behaviors.

item.title: PARP10 condensation inhibits viral replication via targeting NAD<sup>+</sup> homeostasis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78058-y

While specific antiviral mechanisms of certain ADP-ribosyltransferases remain unclear, this study uses vesicular stomatitis virus to reveal that PARP10 forms condensates to amplify enzyme activity. This in turn decreases local NAD+ levels to block viral replication.

item.title: Early insights into predicted efficacy of Ebola monoclonal antibodies for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78077-9

Rapid predictive methods narrow the solution space in an outbreak setting. In this computational study, the authors find that cocktail treatments for Ebola Zaire could be more effective than monotherapies against the 2026 Bundibugyo strain.

item.title: Author Correction: Surfactant-enhanced Cu<sup>δ+</sup> and induced electrostatic forces promote the electrocatalytic deuteron-dechlorination of trichloroacetic acid
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78134-3

Author Correction: Surfactant-enhanced Cuδ+ and induced electrostatic forces promote the electrocatalytic deuteron-dechlorination of trichloroacetic acid

item.title: Emergent memory in cell-like active systems
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77681-z

Living cells can exhibit complex, multi-timescale memory effects influencing their motility and responses to environmental cues. Here, the authors introduce a minimal theoretical framework demonstrating that when active particles, modeled after cells, incorporate internal state dynamics and environmental sensing, emergent environmental memory spontaneously arises.

item.title: Author Correction: A cis-regulatory element of the PHYTOCHROME A gene confers the submergence escape capacity for amphibious plants
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78177-6

Author Correction: A cis-regulatory element of the PHYTOCHROME A gene confers the submergence escape capacity for amphibious plants

item.title: Author Correction: Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase targeted by a Fusarium graminearum effector positively regulates wheat FHB resistance
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78078-8

Author Correction: Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase targeted by a Fusarium graminearum effector positively regulates wheat FHB resistance

item.title: Publisher Correction: Diverse configurations of binary asteroids explained by multi-generation satellites
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78151-2

Publisher Correction: Diverse configurations of binary asteroids explained by multi-generation satellites

item.title: Author Correction: RNA-binding protein RBM3 intrinsically suppresses lung innate lymphoid cell activation and inflammation partially through CysLT1R
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78083-x

Author Correction: RNA-binding protein RBM3 intrinsically suppresses lung innate lymphoid cell activation and inflammation partially through CysLT1R

item.title: Author Correction: Repurposing nuclear receptors for ligand-responsive liquid condensate formation and gene regulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78175-8

Author Correction: Repurposing nuclear receptors for ligand-responsive liquid condensate formation and gene regulation

item.title: Cryo-EM structures of autoinhibited and RNA-activated ZNFX1 helicase
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78145-0

ZNFX1 is an RNA helicase that plays a critical role in host defense against viral infections. Here, the authors reveal how RNA binding remodels autoinhibited ZNFX1 assemblies and activates the helicase for ATP-dependent RNA unwinding.

item.title: Navigational strategy dictates hippocampal representation of space in an everyday memory task
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77885-3

Neurobiology of spatial memory is not fully understood. Using two behavioral tasks, authors demonstrate that the precision of spatial representations is lower in rats using egocentric coordinates, and hippocampus silencing correct only affects goal identification in rats performing allocentrically.

item.title: Spatiotemporal delivery of immune-synapse-stabilizing NK cells for postoperative tumor therapy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77873-7

Here, Li and colleagues report that arming NK cells with surface-anchored, multivalent galectin-3 binding polymers prolongs NK-to-tumor target cell contact and enhances NK cytotoxicity; as well, authors describe that a semi-spike patch for spatiotemporal delivery of armed NK cells in the resection cavity prevents tumor recurrence post-surgery.

item.title: Chronic stress activates a hypothalamic vagal circuit to promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77923-0

Chronic stress can promote hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. Here, the authors show in mice that chronic stress activates a brain-liver signaling circuit that mediates tumor epithelial-macrophage crosstalk and promotes HCC growth.

item.title: Jamming-controlled stochasticity in metal-insulator switching
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76844-2

Phase-transition materials hold promise for neuromorphic technologies, yet their nanoscale switching mechanism remains elusive. Using coherent Bragg scattering, D’Anna et al. show that the initial domain distribution governs stochastic filament formation in VO2 and can be plastically tuned via a jamming transition.

item.title: High-throughput label-free single-cell proteomics enabled by multicolumn NanoLC
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78059-x

Single-cell proteomics reveals cellular diversity, but the throughput has been limited. Here, the authors develop a high-throughput multicolumn nanoLC system that analyzes up to 288 cells per day, identifies ~ 4,000 proteins per cell and profiles inflammatory responses in macrophages.

item.title: SATB1 lowers the T cell receptor signaling threshold for thymocyte positive selection via super-enhancer reprogramming
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78061-3

Satb1 is a chromatin organizer involved in T cell development. Here, the authors demonstrate that Satb1 reorganizes super-enhancer topology to promote the expression of genes associated with thymic positive selection.

item.title: Surface-displayed cholesterol enhances penetration and anti-tumor activity of a platinum nanodrug by targeting NPC1L1-expressing cancer associated fibroblasts
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78085-9

Cancer associated fibroblasts can represent a physical barrier for drug delivery in tumor cells. Here the authors show that, by selectively targeting NPC1L1-cancer associated fibroblasts, surface-displayed cholesterol enhances the delivery of a platinum nanodrug in stroma-rich tumors, restoring anti-tumor efficacy.

item.title: Stepwise pairing and fast transition regulated by recombination drive meiotic chromosome interactions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78036-4

Chromosomes must pair accurately to form healthy reproductive cells. Here, the authors show in mice that this pairing occurs in defined steps controlled by DNA recombination and chromosome-joining structures.

item.title: Record stack durability in industrial solid oxide steam electrolysis through operational control
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78001-1

Demonstration of a long and low degradation solid oxide steam electrolysis experiment for a full SOEC stack, achieving 25,000 hours of operation through AC:DC operation showing potential for low-cost green hydrogen production.

item.title: UpTCR: a unified progressive knowledge transfer foundation model for robust T-cell receptor-antigen binding recognition
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78075-x

Peptides are presented to T Cell receptors (TCR) in the context of human leukocyte antigen (HLA) MHC molecules and the prediction of these peptide sequences are important for vaccines and cancer therapeutics. Here the authors present UpTCR a computational method for learning from incomplete data for TCR-antigen-HLA prediction, considering antigen-HLA binding affinity and specificity and using this tool to predict epitopes in breast cancer patient cohorts.

item.title: Reoviridae-derived short trimerization domain for stabilizing homo-trimerization of vaccine immunogens and therapeutic proteins
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77926-x

In this study, the authors engineer a short trimerization tag for vaccine and therapeutic protein development. The tag enables a trimeric ACE2 decoy that exhibits broad neutralizing activity against coronaviruses and confers protection in animal models.

item.title: Solid–vapor synthesis of dynamic crystalline one-dimensional supramolecular polymers from amorphous macrocycles
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78015-9

Crystalline supramolecular polymers (CSPs) possess ordered polymeric structures for establishing structure–function relationships but most reported CSPs lack dynamic and responsive characteristics intrinsic to supramolecular polymers. Herein the authors report a highly dynamic CSP via a unique solid–vapor host–guest-driven synthesis.

item.title: The biogeography of giant viruses and interactions with Eukaryotes across European lakes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77765-w

Large and giant DNA viruses are widespread in nature but their ecology remains poorly understood in freshwater ecosystems. This study finds that giant viruses are abundant in warmer waters where they are linked to lower primary production.

item.title: A spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic atlas reveals fertilization-induced auxin signaling driving strawberry fruit set and development
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77874-6

Fertilization-triggered fruit set and morphogenesis is a complex process involving multiple cell types. Here the authors use spatial transcriptomics and single nucleus RNA-seq to map fertilization induced changes in woodland strawberry.

item.title: The elongation of Mest transcript into MestXL sustains, but does not initiate, the maternal allele bias of its convergent gene Copg2 during neurogenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77877-3

Precise dosage control of imprinted genes is essential for neurodevelopment, but the mechanisms regulating allele-specific expression remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that maternally biased Copg2 expression arises through a two-step mechanism involving enhancer-mediated maternal activation followed by MestXL-dependent repression of the paternal allele.

item.title: Systemic and Mucosal Antibody Responses Against Neisseria gonorrhoeae (Ng) Outer Membrane Vesicle Antigens following Four-Component Meningococcal Serogroup B (4CMenB) Immunization in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Phase II Trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77936-9

This phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial shows that a two-dose series of 4CMenB vaccine induces both systemic and mucosal IgG responses to Neisseria gonorrhoeae, suggesting a potential role in gonorrhea prevention.
